title: Ordinary henselization under a quasi-finite local map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be primes with $\mathfrak q$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, and assume $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Write $A_{\mathfrak p}^h$ and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ for ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then the canonical map $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\to B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is finite and local, and $B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ is canonically the localization of $A_{\mathfrak p}^h\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q}$ at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}^h$, $H=B_{\mathfrak q}^h$ and $C=R\otimes_A B$. Apply [lem-trf-henselization-tensor-local-comparison] to these ordinary henselizations. Its residue evaluation defines $\mathfrak n\subset C$ with contractions $\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak q$, and $D=C_{\mathfrak n}$. This part of that lemma needs no henselianity assumption on $D$.

The structural map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to R$ is local and $R$ is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-finite-henselian-tensor-factor] to the finite-type map $A\to B$, its quasi-finite point $\mathfrak q$, and the prime $\mathfrak n$ from Step 1. It gives a finite local map $R\to D$ and proves that $D$ is henselian.

Now the conditional comparison in [lem-trf-henselization-tensor-local-comparison] applies: $D\cong H$ compatibly with the canonical map $h:R\to H$ and with $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence $h$ is finite and local, since its target and module action are identified with those of the finite local map $R\to D$ of Step 2. The same lemma identifies $D$ canonically with $(R\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q})_{\mathfrak n_T}$ at the residue-evaluation prime, proving the required canonical localization assertion. Here, with $T=R\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q}$, the prime $\mathfrak n_T$ is the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ in the item: $T/(\mathfrak m_RT+\mathfrak qT)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is a field, so $\mathfrak n_T$ is the unique prime of $T$ over $\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, and it is generated by them.
